speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly how your wrist pain started, when your fever began, and can you show me or describe the appearance of your skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

The combination of migratory arthritis (knee), tenosynovitis (wrist pain), and the history of recent camping in Minnesota (risk for tick-borne illness) alongside sexually active status strongly suggests DGI or Lyme disease; however, the acute onset of joint pain and wrist involvement in a sexually active young male makes DGI the primary clinical suspicion. I am requesting a Gram stain and culture of synovial fluid from the left wrist, as well as a Urine NAAT for *Neisseria gonorrhoeae* and serum Lyme serology.

REQUEST TEST: Synovial Fluid Analysis (Left Wrist), Urine NAAT for Gonorrhea, Lyme_Serology
